Pain de Campagne Baker's Percentage

A rustic loaf that often hides a little whole grain inside mostly white flour. A bit more levain keeps a home bake from taking all day.

Detailed method

One country loaf. Currently 500 g flour, 72% hydration, 25% starter, 2% salt, and 0% yeast. That is 360 g water, 125 g starter, and 10 g salt, 995 g of dough. The starter is itself 100% hydration, the same assumption used for effective hydration. The page shows 75.1% effective hydration. Currently 1 loaf of 995 g. These times assume you only change the flour amount and keep the percentages the same. Still judge the dough by how it looks and feels.

  1. Starter Use 125 g of starter that is bubbly and has about doubled. That starter is part of the gram total.
  2. Mix Stir 500 g flour, 360 g water, the 125 g starter, and 10 g salt until no dry flour remains. At 72% the dough is soft. Aim for about 24°C (75°F).
  3. Bulk Cover it at about 24°C (75°F) for about 3 to 4 hours. Fold it three times in the first 90 minutes. It is ready when it has grown by about half.
  4. Shape Tighten the 995 g into one round and set it seam-side up in a floured basket. This batch is 1 loaf. The default 995 g uses a round lidded pot about 24 cm across and 11 cm high. If you change the amount, use a pot sized to fit, or split the dough.
  5. Proof Cover it for 45 to 75 minutes, until puffy. With 25% starter, bake if the top starts to sink.
  6. Bake Heat the oven to 230°C (450°F) with the lidded pot inside. Place the dough on parchment and lower it, paper and all, into the hot pot. Score a cross or a diamond. Bake 20 minutes covered, then 18 to 24 minutes uncovered, until the crust is deep brown. If you have no lid, invert another pot for the first 20 minutes. Cool on a rack for at least 1 hour.
